content:
Maya (support): heads up — we've got a customer (AcmeRetail) reporting frequent 504s from /v1/rerank when they send batch requests during peak traffic. They say p95 jumps to ~4.8s and then gateway times out. Happening since yesterday afternoon.

Jules (eng-reliability): thanks — do we have request examples and correlation ids?

Maya (support): pasted a sanitized payload they gave: 
```json
{
  "query": "best winter boots for hiking",
  "candidates": ["desc1", "desc2", "desc3", ... up to 200 items],
  "top_k": 10
}
```
They said some batches ~180 candidates. Correlation id: cid=acme-20260312-77a2

Evan (eng-runtime): large candidate sets are expected to stress rerank. Our rerank pipeline does O(N) attention per candidate with some disk reads for model params. 180 seems high but should still fit. Are they doing retries?

Maya (support): yes customer mentioned their client does immediate retries on 5xx with no backoff. They reported seeing a cascade of 502 then 504.

Priya (sre-oncall): I'm pulling metrics. For /v1/rerank the rolling p95 for the last 1h jumped from 450ms -> 4.6s around 2026-03-12T18:20Z. Error rate (5xx) increased from 0.3% -> 6.8%. CPU on rerank-pool nodes spiked to 98% and queue length grew.

Priya (sre-oncall): also seeing gateway (nginx) 504s with upstream_connect_time ~30s. Many upstreams returned 502/503 before hitting 504.

Jules (eng-reliability): possible causes: (1) request size too large causing memory pressure, (2) sync processing queue exhaustion, (3) client retry thundering herd. Check load distribution across pods and whether a single pod was unhealthy.

Evan (eng-runtime): throwing in some logs from a rerank instance (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T18:21:05Z] request cid=acme-20260312-77a2 received, candidates=182, tokens_per_candidate_avg=40
[2026-03-12T18:21:05Z] starting inference batch shard=17, items=182
[2026-03-12T18:21:07Z] gpu_util=98%, mem_free=1.2GB, kv_cache_hits=0
[2026-03-12T18:21:35Z] inference timeout, wall_time=30.4s, error=upstream_timeout
[2026-03-12T18:21:35Z] returning 504 to gateway
```

Maya (support): customer also sent examples of the errors from their side: ``HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout`` and some 502 with body: `{\"error\": \"upstream service error\"}`

Priya (sre-oncall): do we apply request-level timeouts in the rerank workers? What's the per-request infer timeout currently?

Evan (eng-runtime): default worker-level timeout is 28s (we rely on gateway config set to 30s). Long-running large batches can exceed this. There is also a hard global concurrency limiter to avoid OOMs but it uses a FIFO queue which can make p95 spike under backpressure.

Jules (eng-reliability): immediate steps to mitigate for the customer: 1) ask them to reduce candidates to <=64 for now, 2) implement exponential backoff with jitter on client retries, 3) use smaller top_k if possible, 4) set request timeout shorter client-side to avoid cascading.

Maya (support): emailed customer suggested changes above and asked them to enable retry-backoff. They replied that reducing to 64 reduces errors but still sees occasional 504s at peak traffic.

Evan (eng-runtime): ok. Longer-term changes we should consider: - make rerank streaming-friendly / incremental scoring to avoid N^2 work - add per-customer rate limiting and circuit breaker - make worker queue LIFO for latency-sensitive requests - increase worker timeout with careful circuit monitoring - implement adaptive batching that splits huge candidate lists into sub-batches and merges scores.

Jules (eng-reliability): also check kernel-level GPU stalls — if single big request monopolizes GPU and others are queued, p95 will explode. We could add a per-request GPU time quota and preempt long jobs.

Priya (sre-oncall): I can temporarily scale up rerank-pool by +3 nodes (best-effort) to relieve load. Will coordinate during DST window. Scaling should lower queue length and reduce immediate 5xx.

Maya (support): customer asked for SLA note and whether we can prioritize their traffic. They are on a mid-market plan. What's the policy?

Jules (eng-reliability): dedicated capacity is the only way to guarantee isolation. For hosted customers we can offer short-term priority routing (best-effort) via a tagging rule, but must be careful not to starve others. I'll draft an offer: 2-week burst priority with rate limits and monitoring.

Priya (sre-oncall): action items: 1) I scale +3 nodes now (evt id: scale-1779004321-a), 2) enable temporary rate-limiting rule for acme: max_requests_per_minute=1200, 3) add a request size alert (candidates>120) to trigger ops page.

Evan (eng-runtime): action items for runtime: 1) add adaptive-split for candidate lists >80 (server-side), 2) switch FIFO -> LIFO for short-lived workers experiment, 3) add per-request GPU hard-stop at 20s with graceful partial scoring fallback. I'll open PRs for 1 & 2.

Maya (support): I've informed Acme of the scaling and the recommended client changes. They asked for a repro script; can we provide a curl that simulates their load but safe/sampled?

Evan (eng-runtime): yes — gave them a condensed test that uses 60 candidates and exponential backoff. Example curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"best winter boots","candidates":["c1","c2",...],"top_k":10}' \
  --max-time 25
```
Also suggest they implement backoff: sleep = base * 2^attempt + jitter (ms).

Jules (eng-reliability): small note — we should also validate server responses where scores are numeric and bounded. If partial scoring is returned, include a field `partial: true` so clients can handle it. This avoids silent data quality issues.

Priya (sre-oncall): after the scale action p95 dropped to ~520ms and 5xx rate to 0.9% in the last 15m. Still monitoring.

Maya (support): customer confirmed errors dropped significantly after we asked them to lower batch size + we scaled. They want a post-mortem and permanent fix timeline.

Jules (eng-reliability): I'll own the post-mortem and timeline. Tentative plan: short-term server-side adaptive split + client guidance (2 weeks), medium-term LIFO queue + per-request GPU quotas (4-6 weeks), long-term streaming rerank architecture (quarter). I'll create RFC and PM ticket.

support-bot: Ticket created: SPT-4329 (postmortem + mitigation plan).

deploy-bot: Note: no deploys to rerank-pool in flight.

Maya (support): thanks all, keeping Acme updated. Closing the support escalation after postmortem.

Priya (sre-oncall): I'll leave the temporary rate-limit in place for 24h then evaluate. Setting alert: if p95 > 2s for 5m -> page oncall.

Jules (eng-reliability): adding one more verification: audit if any customers are sending >200 candidates regularly; we should proactively contact them.

Maya (support): noted. will pull top customers by candidate-size and loop in AM. :white_check_mark:
